events.evidence: The bank rate which is used in the provision of lender of last resort facility and discount of securities has been kept unchanged at 8 percent.
The bank rate, the policy rate for the purpose of the lender of last resort as well as for the discount of securities, is reduced by 1 percentage point to 7 percent.
The bank rate, applied for the purpose of lender of last resort (LOLR) facility and discount of securities, has been kept unchanged at 7 percent.

events.text: corridor introduced: repo = interbank + 200 bp, deposit collection = interbank - 10 bp
events.evidence: Open Market Transactions Operations Committee (OMTOC) will determine repo rate by adding 200 basis points to the weighted average interbank rate ... The OMTOC will fix deposit collection rate by subtracting 10 basis points from the weighted average interbank rate

The existing standing liquidity facility (SLF) rate as the upper bound of IRC has been reduced from 7 percent to 6.5 per cent and the two-week deposit collection rate as the lower bound has been raised from 3 percent to 3.5 percent.
the two-week deposit collection rate as the lower bound has been raised from 3 percent to 3.5 percent.
The bank rate, applied for the purpose of lender of last resort (LOLR) facility, has been reduced to 6.5 percent from 7 percent.
Policy Rates Fixed Repo Rate (Corridor) 5.0 ... (table in the 2019/20 document covering mid-months of 2018/19)
Repo rate as the policy rate will be reduced from 3.5 percent to 3 percent and deposit collection rate as the lower bound of IRC will be reduced from 2 percent to 1 percent.
deposit collection rate as the lower bound of IRC will be reduced from 2 percent to 1 percent.
Standing Liquidity Facility (SLF) rate as the upper bound of the Interest Rate Corridor (IRC) will remain unchanged at 5 percent.
Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) decreased from 4 percent to 3 percent and bank rate decreased from 6 percent to 5 percent effective from March 29, 2020.
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) has been kept unchanged at 10 percent for commercial banks, 8 percent for development banks and 7 percent for finance companies.
Credit to Deposit cum Core Capital (CCD Ratio) will be increased from 80 percent to 85 percent ... This increase in CCD ratio will remain in effect until mid-July 2021.
Deposit collection rate as the lower bound of IRC will be revised from 1 percent to 2 percent and Repo rate as the policy rate will be revised from 3 percent to 3.5 percent.
Deposit collection rate as the lower bound of IRC will be revised from 1 percent to 2 percent

events.text: CD ratio capped at 90 percent by mid-July 2022 (replaces CCD)
events.evidence: BFIs will be required to limit the credit-deposit ratio (CD Ratio) maximum at 90 percent by mid-July 2022.

events.text: LTV on share-collateral loans may rise 65 to 70 percent
events.evidence: BFIs may increase the LTV ratio from 65 percent to 70 percent on margin nature loans against the collateral of shares.

events.text: valuation: lower of 120-day average close and market price (was 180 days)
events.evidence: 'average closing price of the last 120 days or the prevailing market price of the stock whichever is less' will be considered for the valuation purpose instead of the existing provision of average price of the last 180 days.

In the midterm review of monetary policy, the Standing Liquidity Facility (SLF) rate, policy (repo) rate and deposit collection rate related to Interest Rate Corridor were maintained at 7.0 percent, 5.5 percent and 4.0 percent respectively

events.text: raised 5.5 to 7 percent; bank rate 8.5, deposit collection 5.5
events.evidence: Accordingly, the bank rate has been increased to 8.5 percent, the policy rate to 7.0 percent, and the deposit collection rate to 5.5 percent.
Accordingly, the bank rate has been increased to 8.5 percent
The cash reserve ratio to be maintained by the BFIs will be increased by 1 percentage point to 4 percent with effect from 17 August 2022.

events.text: 12 percent commercial, 10 percent development and finance, from mid-January 2023
events.evidence: the commercial banks need to maintain the statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) of 12 percent and development banks as well as finance companies need to maintain 10 percent from mid-January 2023.

events.text: Rs 120 million per borrower across all institutions
events.evidence: A limit for the margin type of loan against the collateral of shares from a single financial institution or all institutions to be set at Rs.120 million per borrower. (implementation table of the 2022/23 policy)
Considering the domestic and external economic outlook, the policy rate has been reduced by 50 basis points to 6.5 percent.

events.text: reduced 5.5 to 4.5 percent; bank rate 7.5 unchanged
events.evidence: Keeping the bank rate unchanged at 7.5 percent, the deposit collection rate has been reduced to 4.5 percent from 5.5 percent.

events.text: reduced 6.5 to 5.5 percent; bank rate 7, deposit collection 3
events.evidence: first quarter review of the monetary policy reduced bank rate to 7 percent from 7.5 percent, policy rate to 5.5 percent from 6.5 percent and deposit collection rate to 3.0 percent from 4.5 percent.
The bank rate, the upper bound of the interest rate corridor, and the policy rate have been reduced by 50 basis points each to 6.5 percent and 5 percent, respectively.

events.text: Rs 200 million cap scrapped for institutional investors
events.evidence: the current cap of Rs.200 million margin loans against the collateral of shares to be scrapped for the institutional investors, primarily established to invest in the capital market. (implementation table of the 2024/25 policy)
Likewise, the policy rate has been reduced from 5.0 percent to 4.5 percent.

events.text: reduced 6.5 to 6 percent; deposit collection 3 to 2.75
events.evidence: The bank rate, which is considered as the upper bound of the interest rate corridor, has been reduced to 6.0 percent from 6.5 percent, while the deposit collection rate, which is considered as the lower bound of the interest rate corridor, has been reduced to 2.75 percent from 3.0 percent.

events.text: single obligor limit raised Rs 150 million to Rs 250 million
events.evidence: The single obligor limit on margin-nature loans to be extended by the BFIs on share collateral will be increased from Rs.150 million to Rs.250 million.
The risk weight for margin-type loans has been reduced from 125 percent to 100 percent.
